content.body:
Probably the most famous tank of WW2, the Tiger had a long development. From an original design for a modest 33 ton "breakthrough" tank, it ballooned to a 57 ton behemoth after humbling first encounters with the Russian T34. Despite its heavy armor and superb gun, the Tiger's initial performance in combat was unimpressive, suffering extensive mechanical breakdowns due to a rushed deployment. After the teething problems were largely solved, the Tiger earned its fearsome reputation at the hands of audacious commanders like Michael Wittman: his skilled crew was credited with knocking out 141 tanks and 132 AT guns.
The Tiger is an outstanding vehicle, close to undefeatable by any other tank in the game if used properly. The exceptionally good gun means that anytime you engage a target at less than 500 m, you are handing them a significant chance they would not otherwise ever have and foolishly counteracting your own strength. Keep your very thick front armor in mind at all times - facing an enemy will make you almost invulnerable to all but the very best Allied anti-tank guns, basically those 76 mm or more in caliber or the high velocity 6 pounder if he gets close enough to you.
But beware of aircraft - you are a high value target that enemy pilots will be searching constantly for. The Tiger's massive gun means a relatively slow turret speed, but this also means that the Tiger is a particularly effective tank for multicrewing if you follow the famous Wittmans's example. He developed the clever and expedient maneuver of "assisted slewing," where the driver would spin the tank as hard as possible while the slower turret turned in the same direction, giving the tank an effective turret slew rate much higher than available by simply traversing the gun - probably worth practicing with a regular multicrew buddy.
